topic: Adjusting frequency calculation for unique users
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on discrepancies in frequency calculations, particularly concerning unique users (uniques) and traffic volume when comparing data before and after mirroring. A key concern was that the calculated level of uniques appeared lower post-mirroring than expected, despite similar user bases.

To address this, a consensus was reached to implement a new formula for calculating uniques based on multiplying frequency by the number of facilities (`n`). This method aims to ensure consistent unique counts regardless of the selected facility count (from 1 to 8).

It was decided that someone should run their updated model and review the period following the mirroring event. If this approach proves successful, the historical calculation for uniques should also be adjusted accordingly.
decisions: Implement a formula multiplying frequency by the number of facilities (n) to calculate unique users.
Review the performance of the new model in the post-mirroring period.
If the new method is validated, apply it retroactively to historical data.
action_items: Someone needs to run and validate their updated model for the period after mirroring (starting November 5th).
